A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UG framework and contain readable main text and appendices A–I. Equations, tables, figures and relocated material can be matched reliably, with no material comparison gaps.

before.justification: V2 reports original evaluations of UG-Search, UG-Sample and UG-Ground, alongside efficiency experiments, ablations and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds scoring-method comparisons, localization-precision measurements and performance–latency experiments in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The entropy-based crop/frame selection, BRC scoring, Kadane-based grounding and existing efficiency variants remain unchanged. UG-Sample+AKS already appeared in v2; v3 expands its explanation. New scoring alternatives serve as experimental comparators.

E1.justification: The image/video coverage and three principal tasks are retained. Appendix G.3 uses KFS-Bench annotations for a subset of the existing Video-MME data, adding a selection-precision diagnostic rather than a distinct input domain or task.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds VTG-GPT, TFVTG and TAG as training-free grounding comparators. Appendix G adds binary relevance, self-reported confidence and standalone SigLIP scoring comparisons, plus Majority-of-N, Best-of-N, their randomized-input variants and TimeSearch-R. This substantially expands the comparison methods beyond v2.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs measure top-1 target-selection precision and compare fixed-input versus randomized-input answer sampling. Appendix G.4 sweeps N={4,8,16,32,64}, crop sizes and candidate-frame budgets, with reported forward-pass matching. Existing benchmark settings are retained; these are additional protocols.

E4.justification: New Sections G.2–G.4 test the choice of scoring signal, whether selected inputs contain the target, and the performance–latency trade-off against alternative uses of inference compute. These substantially extend the retained granularity, scaling, efficiency and robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or explicit significance-testing procedures. Existing entropy distributions and correlation analyses are retained. The new confidence-scoring experiments do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Previously reported UG scores remain unchanged, but Table 5 adds grounding-baseline results, Tables 10 and 12 add scoring and precision results, and Figure 6 adds performance–latency curves. For example, new entropy-selection precision is 79.6% on V*Bench and 44.7% on Video-MMEkfs, versus 0.0% and 4.2% for self-reported confidence.

T1.justification: The entropy/BRC definitions and Appendix C's information-bottleneck derivation, calibration assumption, Theorem 1 and proof are unchanged. The added top-1 precision evaluation does not revise the formal theory.

C1.justification: The introduction removes the explicit model-agnostic characterization, slightly softening its stated generality. The abstract, three contributions and conclusion otherwise retain the same training-free framework, three-task scope and competitive-performance claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly attributes the MLVU weakness to insufficient coverage of distributed counting events and explains the existing AKS hybrid's role. Section 4.5 clarifies inference costs and query-agnostic detector failures. Appendix G interprets confidence-scoring failures through overconfidence and poor discrimination.

D1.justification: Table 11 supplies binary-relevance and 0–10 confidence prompt templates. Appendix G identifies the keyframe-annotation source and documents sampling rules and budget sweeps. Existing implementation defaults, batching, caching, hardware information and code-access instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds discussion and citations for training-free grounding methods, TimeSearch-R, KFS-Bench and confidence elicitation, while removing the COSMOS, FLAIR and original CLIP reference entries. These are targeted literature updates; the central positioning of uncertainty as proactive guidance is retained.

P1.justification: V3 locally rewrites the comparison and efficiency discussions, adds keywords and a supplementary contents list, and introduces Sections G.2–G.4. Most prose and the overall section organization remain intact; the new scientific content does not constitute a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 10–12 and Figure 6, groups Table 5 by method category and removes its stray 1.2EM header text. Several existing displays move closer to their discussions. Earlier Tables 10–12 and Figures 6–9 are retained under new numbering, with their substantive displays unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added scoring controls, localization-precision evidence and compute comparisons in G.2–G.4 strengthen the existing empirical case. Training-free grounding comparators and clearer discussion of MLVU coverage and inference costs also improve assessment of the method. These provide a focused quality gain over an already extensive study, while experimental uncertainty reporting and the theoretical assumptions remain unchanged.
